earlier_scan.source_named: David Beck 2025 (work on Totonacan subclassification cited on Glottolog tecp1235); no dedicated Tecpatlan Totonac phonology found online
earlier_scan.note: Totonacan descriptions plausibly cover stress; Tecpatlan variety source not reachable.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page tecp1235 (Hammarström et al.), with linked reference records 700656 (Beck 2025 'Totonacan languages', Mouton) and 569683 (Campbell et al. 2022 ElCat); Glottolog reference search q=Tecpatlán
sources.note: No descriptive references at all for tecp1235 (only Ethnologue editions, ISO CR, ElCat); 'Comments on subclassification: David Beck 2025' = Beck's Totonacan overview chapter in Wichmann (ed.), typed overview;comparative. Reference search for 'Tecpatlán' returns nothing.

sources.citation: García-Vega, Michelle. 2022. Morphology of Zihuateutla Totonac. PhD dissertation, University of Alberta (Scholaris hdl 123456789/74436). Sister Northern Totonac language, Zihuateutla municipality (the municipality Tecpatlán lies).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: NOT about Tecpatlán (0 mentions). For Zihuateutla Totonac, §2.2 'Stress' pp. 47-53: 'stress in ZT is fairly regular and predictable, falling on the ultimate or the penultimate syllable for all lexical classes.. stress the penultimate syllable in words ending in a light syllable.. and stress falls on the ultimate syllable of words ending in a heavy syllable that is, words ending in a long vowel or closed syllable' (p. 53); exceptions: agentive nominalizer attracts stress, deictic adverbs final, stem-final verbs final; auditory judgments of citation forms.

sources.citation: Beck, David. 2008. Ideophones, adverbs, and predicate qualification in Upper Necaxa Totonac. IJAL 74(1): 1-46 (fn. 2, p. 2) — already held by the project from the patl1234 check
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress section (§2.3, p. 15) is for Upper Necaxa only. Fn. 2: Tecpatlán 'differs significantly from the Totonac of Patla and Chicontla both lexically and phonologically.. so it seems best to exclude Tecpatlán from Upper Necaxa Totonac' — i.e. the UNT stress statement is explicitly not claimed for Tecpatlán.

sources.citation: Beck, David. Homepage publication list, https://sites.ualberta.ca/~dbeck/
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Tecpatlán item; lists Beck 2024 'Totonacan languages' (Wichmann ed., Mouton, 555-597) and Beck 2023 'Morphological diffusion and the internal sub-grouping of Central Totonac' (LDC 13(3)) as the only family-wide works.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Tecpatlán Totonac' (stub) and 'Totonac language'; Wikidata Q7692795; SIL Mexico 'Familia totonaca' page; UAlberta Scholaris search 'Totonac' (27 items); CrossRef/Semantic Scholar/archive.org searches for 'Tecpatlán Totonac'
sources.note: No Tecpatlán-specific linguistic content anywhere; Wikipedia's Totonac phonology section is Huehuetla; no repository, CrossRef, Semantic Scholar or archive.org item has 'Tecpatlán Totonac' in its title. Beck's 2011 and 2017 UAlberta talk slides on Northern/Central Totonac exist on Scholaris but are access-restricted (not reachable by automated download).

sources.citation: Ethnologue 26th ed. (Eberhard, Simons & Fennig eds. 2023), entry 'Totonac, Tecpatlán' [tcw], free view via Internet Archive copy 2023-03-09
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology. Autonyms 'Tachiwiin, Tutunakuj'; 'Existing Content: NT (1999)'; endangered; <10K speakers. The live ethnologue.com page is JS/paywall-blocked.

sources.citation: Beck, David. 2012. Appendix: comparative morphological tables (author's English translation of 'Apéndice: Tablas de morfología comparativa', in P. Levy & D. Beck (eds.), Las lenguas totonacas y tepehuas: Textos y otros materiales para su estudio, 587-596. Mexico: UNAM).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative morphology only; columns Tl, H, Pf, M, CX, U, FM, Ol, On, P — no Tecpatlán data. One passing remark (p. 169 of text dump): a morphological change 'in some languages.. also involves a leftward movement of stress' (not about Tecpatlán).

sources.citation: Beck, David. 2007. ISO 639-3 Request for New Language Code Element: Tecpatlán Totonac (tcw), associated with CR 2006-085. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Location (village of Tecpatlán plus possibly two smaller communities, valley of a tributary of the Necaxa River), ~540 speakers per INEGI, community also bilingual in Nahuatl; 'Knowledge from published sources' left blank; written literature: 'none'; closest language: 'unknown'.

sources.citation: Beck, David (with Yvonne Lam). 2006. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2006-085: split [tot] Patla-Chicontla Totonac into Upper Necaxa Totonac [tku] and Tecpatlán Totonac [tcw]. SIL International ISO 639-3 Registration Authority, 7 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only Tecpatlán-specific phonological remarks anywhere: Tecpatlán 'has also undergone a shift of /w/ to /b/', shares lenition of *q to glottal stop with Upper Necaxa but 'retains /q/ in at least some lexical items'; many lexical differences; Beck 'recorded a short text in Tecpatlán' in 2006 (unpublished).

sources.citation: Beck, David. Upper Necaxa Totonac Project website (University of Alberta), pages 'Totonacan languages', 'Zihuateutla Totonac', 'Publications', 'Sound system', 'Language vitality' (all 33 pages pulled via WP REST API)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Tecpatlán stress. Places Tecpatlán in Northern Central Totonac (Upper Necaxa, Tecpatlán, Zihuateutla, Apapantilla, Pantepec, Coahuitlán) citing 'Moore 2017; Beck to appear'; the publications list contains no Tecpatlán-specific work; only a Tecpatlán teacher named among bilingual-education participants.

sources.citation: Beck, David. 2024. Totonacan languages. In Søren Wichmann (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of Mexico and Northern Central America: A Comprehensive Guide, 555-598. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Family overview by the only linguist who has worked in Tecpatlán; Glottolog attaches it to tecp1235; most likely place for a family-level statement on Totonacan stress and any remark on Northern varieties including Tecpatlán. Overview, not a Tecpatlán description.

sources.citation: Beck, David. 2023. Morphological diffusion and the internal subgrouping of Central Totonac. Language Dynamics and Change 13(3)/14(1): 1-52.

Talk slides (Scholaris hdl 123456789/30754).

sources.citation: Beck, David. 2006. Unpublished Tecpatlán recording ('a short text in Tecpatlán') and preliminary dialect survey of Patla, Chicontla, Cacahuatlán and Tecpatlán (mentioned in ISO CR 2006-085 §5a).

sources.note: The only primary Tecpatlán data known to exist; unpublished, held by the author (University of Alberta). A direct ask to David Beck is the realistic route to any stress statement for this variety.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives records: Bishop, Ruth G. 1990. Glossed texts in Patla Totonac (38 pp., tagged Upper Necaxa Totonac [tku]); Button, Ella Marie & Ruth G. Bishop. 1997. El alfabeto totonaco de Patla y Chicontla (4 pp., tku). Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
